hints: Combine the two fractions and set the result equal to $1/t$.
Reduce to an equation in $t^2$, then use $t>0$ for $0^\circ<\theta<90^\circ$ before applying inverse tangent.
walkthrough:
Apply the compound angle formulas for tangent with $\tan 60^\circ = \sqrt{3}$:
$$\tan(\theta + 60^\circ) = \dfrac{\tan\theta + \tan 60^\circ}{1 - \tan\theta\tan 60^\circ} = \dfrac{\tan\theta + \sqrt{3}}{1 - \sqrt{3}\tan\theta}$$
$$\tan(\theta - 60^\circ) = \dfrac{\tan\theta - \tan 60^\circ}{1 + \tan\theta\tan 60^\circ} = \dfrac{\tan\theta - \sqrt{3}}{1 + \sqrt{3}\tan\theta}$$

Add the two tangent terms over a common denominator $(1 - \sqrt{3}\tan\theta)(1 + \sqrt{3}\tan\theta) = 1 - 3\tan^2\theta$:
$$\text{LHS} = \dfrac{(\tan\theta + \sqrt{3})(1 + \sqrt{3}\tan\theta) + (\tan\theta - \sqrt{3})(1 - \sqrt{3}\tan\theta)}{1 - 3\tan^2\theta}$$

Express $\cot\theta$ as $\dfrac{1}{\tan\theta}$ and equate to the simplified left-hand side:
$$\dfrac{8\tan\theta}{1 - 3\tan^2\theta} = \dfrac{1}{\tan\theta}$$

Cross-multiply to form an equation in $\tan^2\theta$:
$$8\tan^2\theta = 1 - 3\tan^2\theta \implies 11\tan^2\theta = 1$$

Solve for $\tan^2\theta$ and take the square root:
$$\tan^2\theta = \dfrac{1}{11} \implies \tan\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{11}}$$
(The negative root is rejected since $0^\circ < \theta < 90^\circ$ requires $\tan\theta > 0$).

ai_rubric.Solving Trigonometric Equations: Applies the $\tan(A\pm B)$ formula and expresses the left-hand side in terms of $\tan\theta$. Using $\tan60^\circ=\sqrt3$ and $\cot\theta=1/\tan\theta$, Derives an equation in $\tan\theta$. The final result is $\theta=16.8^\circ$.
